column1: # What the game's 413 script functions do: all of them, from main.dol's table. name, short name, system, how sure, what it does, arguments.
# proved: seen in the disc's data against a save's memory or a run, or data and code agree. read: read from its disassembly, nothing run. guess: from how scripts use it.
# Each was read, then checked by a skeptic. Add to this as you learn. Never promote a guess without saying what proved it.

column5: fn0() at 0x80168C24: returns the u16 at +2 of the running script's slot in 0x805CAA40, 0 if none (r2-22096 is 0.0). Layout checked in slots 2 and 3. With one argument it reads argument index 2, not 1 (0x80168C94); index 2 is past the top, so 0x801633D8 gives nothing and 0x80163510 returns r2-22160, 0.0, so it looks for id 0: an empty slot (step 0) or none (0). So the only such call, L06/2076 fn0(1783), does not read 1783 and gives 0 (read from code, not run); more than 1 argument is an error.

fn1(step[, script]) at 0x80168B64: 0x80163C6C(script, step, -1), writes the u16 at +2 of the script's 8-byte slot in the 10-slot table at 0x805CAA40, taking the first empty slot if the script has none (0x80163D8C writes the id); a negative step is not written (0x80163D90). Script defaults to the running one (r13-23228). Live table: slot3 (2133, step 4), slot2 (2129, step 1); those scripts have fn1(4) and fn1(1). L08/2074 fn1(0, 342) sets another script's step.

fn2(n): how slowly the camera target closes on its destination. Writes +48 of 0x80602C28 (target destination) and 0x806037D8 (eye current) via 0x801EB974. The step does value -= (value-destination)/+48 of the current record (0x801EBFD4-0x801EBFE4), so n is a divisor, not a frame count; current +48 itself eases to the destination's (0x801EC060). Live slot1: current 0x80603860 has +112 = 0x80602C28, whose position is the target shown at 0x803012E0, +48 20; the currents' +48 is 19.9993, easing. Corrects camera_time_a. Default 32 (r2-18968, 0x801EB7F8). Usually fn3(n) fn2(n) after fn8. 818 calls, 589 are fn2(20).

fn3(n): as fn2 for the eye. Writes +48 of 0x80603288 (eye destination) and 0x80603860 (target current) via 0x801EB974. Same divisor rule as fn2. Live slot1: current 0x806037D8 has +112 = 0x80603288, whose position is the eye 470,-145,359, +48 20. Each of fn2 and fn3 sets one current record of the other's pair directly. Corrects camera_time_b. Often alone after fn8: L00/1161 fn8(565170590,0,2,0,0) fn3(20). 1087 calls, 753 are fn3(20).

fn4(n): sets +56 of the eye record 0x80603288 (0x80168504 -> 0x801EB97C). 0x801EC71C passes +56 to 0x801EC588, which adds n times the vector at character+12 (0x80118938) to the followed character's point (0x801EC6BC-0x801EC6DC). That +12 is motion, and so the name camera_lead, is a reading. Default 0.0 (r2-18964, 0x801EB7FC). All 19 calls are fn4(0), 15 on the script's first line: L00/1161 fn4(0) fn8(...) fn3(20). No nonzero value in any script.

fn5(n) at 0x80168594. No script calls it. Calls 0x801EB844(0x80603288, n): if n is nonzero and there is a player (r13-26524), stores at +84 the unit vector to the eye slot from the point +116 points at (0x80602C28, the look-at record, in slots 1, 2, 3, 7), or from the player if +116 is 0; then n at +60 (0 if the vector is zero). 0x801EC754 then builds its result from that vector times +40, plus +44 on z, added to the +116 point, instead of turning (0,+40,+44) with the facing. That result only reaches the eye when +36 is 0 or 1 (0x801ECA04, 0x801ECA40); see fn6. Returns nothing.

fn6(distance) at 0x8016862C, through 0x801EB830: float at 0x80603288+40 on the eye slot (0x80603178 array, entry 2), only while r13-26524 (player) is set. 0x801EC754 uses it as the follow offset's distance (y of the offset, 0x801EC794). 750 in slots 1, 2, 3, 7. The offset goes on from 0x801EC9AC only when +36 is 0 or 1; +36 is 2 in those saves, where 0x801ECA18 ignores it, so a call in that mode changes nothing until the mode changes (fn32 sets 0). Only script: L07/2687 fn6(50) three times, each before fn8, fn6(600) later.

fn7(height) at 0x801686BC, through 0x801EB81C: float at 0x80603288+44, the follow offset's height in 0x801EC754 (z of the offset, 0x801EC79C). 400 in slots 1, 2, 3, 7. Same limit as fn6: not used while +36 is 2, as it is in those saves. No script calls it.

fn8(camera hash, a, b, c, d): selects a room camera for the eye record 0x80603288 and its linked target record 0x80602C28 (+116). Live slot1: eye 470,-145,359 and target -112,85,283 equal the view at 0x803012E0, and 470,-145,359 is room 147's Camera01. Read from 0x801EE764 and 0x801EE43C: a nonzero makes the target follow the player (r13-26524, 0x801EE694); b is the eye's mode at +36 (1 0x801ED0FC, 2 0x801ED6F4, else 0x801EDA40; live slot1 eye +36=2); c=0 cuts: sets +64 of 0x806037D8 (0x801EE8A4), snapping that frame (0x801EBA58); c not 0 blends; d nonzero resets both records first (0x801EB7A0), but d is 0 in every script call. A hash not found does nothing (0x801EE924). All 2801 calls: fn8(h,0,2,1,0) 821, fn8(h,0,0,0,0) 770, fn8(h,0,2,0,0) 535, fn8(h,0,0,1,0) 511, fn8(h,1,0,1,0) 116, fn8(h,1,0,0,0) 43, with locals 5.
column6: camera hash, a, b, c, d

column5: fn10(camera hash, reverse, c): selects a camera and starts its own path. Corrects camera_set2. Same 0x801EE8E0 as fn8 but its path argument is 1, so 0x801EE43C takes the branch at 0x801EE498: reverse=0 runs forward (+24=+1), nonzero backward (+24=-1), start from 0x801EE108, 0x801EE180, 0x801EE1F0. Falls to the fixed branch if the camera has no path counts (entry +96, +104). Of its calls, 48 name a camera rooms. Every literal fn10 hash is a room camera (2,177 are read now). c as in fn8. All 237 calls pass reverse 0, so backward is never used by a script; c is 0 in 214, 1 in 23.

fn11(script): the script the camera runs when it has arrived. Replaces camera_other. 0x80166BA4 -> 0x801ED0D4 stores it at 0x80603288+68. The step 0x801EBF4C fires it for the eye only (the record with +116, 0x801EC144), once the current position is within one step of the destination (each delta / +48 truncates to 0, 0x801EC108-0x801EC140) and then either eye and target are both in state +32 = 4 or 5 (0x801EC150-0x801EC174; the path stepper sets 4 at its end, 0x801ECC74; a pending +128 callback goes first, 0x801EC178) or the eye is in state 3, which becomes 2 (0x801EC1D0-0x801EC1E0). It calls 0x801642D4(script,0,0) and clears it. Corrects 'runs next': it waits for that. Selecting a camera with path counts clears it (0x801EE48C), so it has to come after fn10. All 99 calls name the calling script's own id, 84 straight after fn10: L00/1351 fn10(248020730,0,0) fn11(1351) fn36(60) fn1(3). Not watched in a run.

fn12(uid, anim, flags, marker userdata, turn rate degrees): queues an animation that moves to a marker, returns its slot as a handle (0 if uid not found or no slot). 0x80167024 -> 0x80166E50 with r4=1 (its only call, so the r4=0 play-now branch 0x80122BB0 is dead) -> 0x80122CBC: 0x801228D0 takes the next of 8 272-byte slots at character+64, 0x8012312C fills it, 0x80122E20 stores the target at +204, 0x80122FE8 the rate, unless flag 0x40 is set (0x80122D28). Priority is fixed at 5 (0x80122D14, see fn14). Marker is 3 s16 from fn63. Degrees x r2-22108 (live 0.01745). L00/1023: L5=fn184(L0,Marker) fn15(L0,2,5,L5,10) L6=fn12(L0,2,1,Marker,10) fn17(L6,1023). 76 calls.
column6: uid, anim, flags, marker userdata, turn rate degrees

column5: fn13(uid, anim, flags, priority): queues an animation after the current one, returns the slot as a handle. Corrects blend: see fn14. With no slot it raises a script error 'Could not Queue anim' (0x80253FE0) rather than just logging: 0x8015CA30 -> 0x80159E28 -> 0x80159E68, which longjmps (0x800EE954), so the script stops there. 0x8016704C -> 0x80122A2C: next slot from 0x801228D0, 0x8012312C sets anim +240, flags +244, priority +250, then state +252=2. No check that the uid was found. L03/2205: L1=fn13(L0,115,32,15). All 21 calls pass priority 15.

fn14(uid, anim, flags, priority): plays an animation in the current slot now if the running one lets it, returns the slot as a handle, 0 if no uid, no character+60, or refused. Corrects blend: +250 is a priority. 0x80167180 -> 0x80122920: 0x80122274 (slot index at +2176), 0x80123070 decides, 0x8012312C fills, 0x80123224 starts. 0x80123070 replaces a slot that is playing (+252 bit 4) only if priority > +250, or the same anim with flag 0x10, or equal priority and a different anim with flag 0x20; otherwise refused, and for the same anim at equal priority only flags +244 change (0x80122988-0x801229B4). 0x80123730 also tests +250 < 4 before a queued animation cuts in. Slot layout seen live in slot1, slot3, slot7: player's slot 0 has anim 15, flags 0x21, priority 1, state 4; slots 1-7 state 1, anim -1. All 49 script calls pass 15: fn14(L2,16,0,15), fn14(SummonedMonster,15,1,15), fn17(fn14(L2,124,32,15),1438); fn17 doesn't check for a 0 handle (0x80167628-0x80167658). What each anim id and the other flags are: not found here.

fn15(uid, anim, flags, angle degrees, turn rate degrees): queues an animation that turns to a heading, returns its slot. With no slot it raises a script error 'Could not Queue seek mode' (0x80253FF8) that stops the script, as in fn13. 0x801672A8 -> 0x80122F38 -> 0x80122FE8: heading +192, rate +188, +248 |= 2. Priority fixed at 5 (0x80122F9C, see fn14). All 76 calls are anim 2 flags 5, the angle often from fn184: L00/1023 fn15(L0,2,5,L5,10), then fn12. L00/1363 fn15(L0,2,5,180,20).
column6: uid, anim, flags, angle degrees, turn rate degrees

column5: fn16(handle, script, frame): runs the script when the animation reaches that frame. 0x80167510 -> 0x80121C08 adds an event on the slot (callback 0x80168368, script at +56, frame<<17 at +112; room for 14, no limit check); 0x80168368 calls 0x801642D4(script, character, 0); the tick compares current time with +112 at 0x80124330 and fires once (flag bit at slot+258, 0x80124370). Only call: L03/2205 fn16(L1,2205,-2), after L1=fn13(L0,115,32,15); -2 is below any forward time, so read as firing on the first tick that slot is current, not seen in a run.

fn17(handle, script): runs the script when that animation finishes. 0x801675D4 -> 0x8012206C stores callback 0x80168368 at slot+176, script at +180; fired at 0x801237EC-0x80123804 through 0x801DCAE4. The usual way a script waits on a walk: L00/1023 L6=fn12(...) fn17(L6,1023) fn1(1). All 61 calls with a literal id name the calling script itself.

fn19(uid, on): on the character's bone-turning block at +656. Read at 0x8016771C: on=1 clears bit 32 of block+84 (0x801295F4); on=0 calls 0x80129878(char,1) then sets bit 32. The block holds a world point at +0 and up to 4 bone ids at +12 with a float each at +28 (live slot3 player: bones 1,0,-1,-1; 0.0131, 0.0175). That this is the head looking at things is a guess. Scripts: fn19(L0,0) at a scene's start, fn19(L0,1) at its end (L00/864, L06/1518). 67 calls.

fn20(uid, on, bit): mask for the same +656 block as fn19. Read at 0x801677F8: on=1 clears 1<<bit in block+76, bit<0 clears all (0x8012969C, 0x80129658); on=0 sets it, bit<0 sets 255, and calls 0x80129878 if bit equals block+85 or bit<0. What each bit is: not found; scripts use 1 and 4 only: L03/1289 fn20(L0,0,1), L03/1290 fn20(L0,1,1), L01/1265 fn20(L0,0,4). 18 calls.

fn21(0) holds play, fn21(1) lets go. 0x8016820C: with 0 and a player (r13-26524) adds 4 to their animation flags (0x80122514, 0x801223B8), then calls 0x80199EA0(arg). On 0 that sets +16 of the channels at r13-23060, -23052 to 0x0FFFFFFF (0x8013DBC8); on nonzero it zeroes them (0x8013DBC0); -23056 +16 is set either way (0x80199ED0). It also sets busy bit 2 of r13-23344 through 0x801556CC, cleared only on arg 1 (0x80199F14-0x80199F34); that word is asked at 0x8000749C before the player's controller runs (docs/coop-tome-pickups.md, read not run). 0x80199EA0 has 53 callers, so fn21 is not the only hold. Lowered from proved: no save is in a held state (14 saves: busy word 0, -23060 +16 is 0), and the urn run is only as reported in docs/coop-next-session.md and docs/coop-no-pause.md (logs/run-20261103-134455-urn-nopause), which say the channels as the cause is inferred; not re-checked here. 564 fn21(0), 310 fn21(1), 305 scripts counting each level. L03/1429 lines 78, 98.

Corrects hide_hud. fn22(on, keep), no return, 988 calls, (1,1) 435, (0,1) 461, (1,0) 51, (0,0) 41. keep is 1 or not: the native passes bit 0 only if arg 2 is exactly 1. Calls 0x80042974: when on and not keep calls 0x801C5118(1), which looks for a cast and ends it through 0x801C4F08 (hle.c lists it in kCastEnds; that a cast is what it ends is from that list); when on ORs 4 into the player's flags (0x801223B8), not when off; r13-23280=on (0x80152204); 0x80199EA0(!on), the play hold, if there's a player; bit 32 of r13-23344; r13-21900=on; r13-25696=on; zones off with 0x8019C088(!on); bit 1 of r13-24048; when on 0x801EC3A0, 0x801EEE90(2,..), 0x801EEB58(2), when off 0x801EEE90(2, another triple) and 0x80134D48(player). 0x801EEB58 and 0x801EEE90 write the camera records docs/game/systems/camera.md places at 0x80602B18. Nothing in it touches the HUD directly

fn23(region hash), returns 1 or nil. Hash through 0x800EE044, then walks the room's zones from 0x80155130(2) (count +176, list +180, 116 bytes each): 1 if +44 is the hash and +104 bit 0 is set. The bit's writer 0x80134684 uses mask 1 when its r6 is 0 and 2 otherwise, and 0x80134D80 makes r6 'thing isn't the player' (r13-26524). COOP_ZONE_INSIDE in hle.c names +104; docs/coop-failed-attempts.md traces it. Saves: slot1 has one zone with bit 0, hash 0xCB0F3B3E (3406773054, which 48 fn23 calls ask), slot3 one with word 3. So it asks about the player only: for another thing use fn181. 1099 calls in 390 scripts

Corrects used_thing. fn25(), no arguments, returns r13-23276, the current room (0x8016A9D4). Saves: slot1 147, slot2 147, slot3 21, slot7 155, slot10 115; the task names slot1 as room 147. Scripts' 153 and 155 in 1429 are rooms: `if fn25() ~= 155`. 1298 calls in 454 scripts. the old items page calling it what a thing had used on it is wrong

fn26(0|1), no return, other values give 'Invalid Region Setting %d (must be 0 or 1)' (0x80254348), a Lua error. 0x8019C088 stores r13-23040. 0x8019C098 reads it at 0x80134A80 and 0x80134F1C, both branching past their zone loop when 0. Not every zone walk asks: 0x80134D48 (run when fn22 or fn139 ends) and fn181's 0x801FAD9C don't. Also written by fn22 and fn139 as !on. All saves read 1. 31 calls each way: fn26(0) then fn132 in L00/1023

fn27(uid, marker userdata): moves a character to the marker at once. 0x8016794C: 0x8016E764 turns the marker's 3 s16 into floats, 0x80118248 writes character+0,+4,+8 (live slot1 player -663.7,220.9,-48.0). Does nothing if uid not found. L06/1518: fn27(L0,fn63(3816166214)) fn123(L0,L1) with L1=fn64(same hash). 104 calls.

fn28(uid, part, on): shows or hides a body part. The game's own error text names it: 'Char_Show_Body_Part: No Game object with iUID = %d' (0x80254014). 0x80167ACC -> 0x801258BC: part record at character+576 [part], bit 0 of +8, and each listed bone's word at character+384 + 8*bone, following sub-parts. On=1 also clears bit 0 of up to two more bones named at +12, +13 of the part's data (0x80125990-0x801259E0). A uid not found raises that text as a script error, which stops the script (0x80167B90-0x80167BA4, as in fn13). L04/1869: fn28(L0,8,1) fn28(L0,9,0). Part 15 is 111 of 157 calls; what it is: not found.

fn29(flag, on) at 0x80168EE8: on 0 clears through 0x801DC1D0, otherwise sets through 0x801DC1A4 (not 0 or 1 prints "Bit value must be 0 or 1" and still sets). Bits at *(r13-26528)+4, flag>>5 words, bit flag&31; base 0x80705BE0 in slots 1, 2, 3, 7. Flag 266 is on in slot2 at that bit, as docs/coop-tome-pickups.md logged 1429 setting it.
fn30(flag) at 0x80168FD8: returns 1 or 0 through 0x801DC22C, same bits as fn29. Flag 266 by this layout is 0 in slot1 and 1 in slot2 (the bits read from the save; the function itself was not run).
fn31(flag) at 0x80169080: flips the bit through 0x801DC1F4 and returns the new value, 1 or 0. No script calls it.

fn32() at 0x801688B8, 0 arguments. 0x801EB7A0(0x80603288, 0) puts the eye slot back to defaults: +36=0, +40=750, +44=400, +48=32, +52=60, +56=0, +60=0, +68=0 (floats from r2-18976..-18960, r2 0x80628460). +36 is the mode tested at 0x801EC9F0: 2 in slots 1, 2, 3, 7, so this changes it. +52 holds the field of view: 65.25, 65.25, 64.999, 60.0 in those saves, the same as the view's FOV at 0x803012E0+48. +48 is 20 in them, not 32. Undoes fn5, fn6, fn7. Scripts call it around a door: L08/435 fn32() fn71(213) fn66(213,...), L08/249 fn66 then fn32.
fn33() at 0x8016893C: the same instructions as fn32, same target 0x80603288, same 0x801EB7A0(...,0). No script calls it.

fn34() at 0x80168DFC, 0 arguments: copies the running script (r13-23228) to r13-23220. 0x80164470 reads that word when a script returns and, if nonzero, runs it through 0x801642D4 at once. So fn1(4) fn34() (L00/129) goes straight on to the next step. Corrects stop_self: it does not stop anything.

fn35(on[, script]) at 0x80168D40: 0x80163F88 writes on to the u16 at +6 of the slot. 0x80163F04(1) (called at 0x8015213C) and 0x80163E84 clear a slot only when +6 is 0, so 1 keeps the script's step through those clears. 379 fn35(1) and 354 fn35(0) in scripts, e.g. L00/1599 fn1(2) fn35(1) ed55(114), then fn35(0) fn66. Corrects script_timer: it is not a timer.

fn36(frames[, script]), no return. 0x80163C6C(script, -1, frames), script being the current one (r13-23228) unless a second argument names another; any other argument count is a Lua error. It doesn't pause the script: the native returns and the lines after it run (L11/1590 `fn36(100) fn1(1)`), and the wait is until that script next runs from the top. Only one call has two: fn36(1, 2776) in L12/2479. Same reading as primitives.tsv, second argument added

fn39(handle, rate) at 0x80169440: handle through 0x801F5F88 then 0x801F633C (errors "Couldn't Find GO for UID %i", "Couldn't Find Char for UID %i GO %p"). Writes rate to the current animation block +200 (0x80122B3C, 0x80122B2C) and character +600 (0x80118CBC). 0x80123180 copies +600 to +200 for a new block; 0x8012376C passes +200 to 0x8011FF74, which gives it to 0x8011FE38: each pass the block's clock +0 moves by rate times its direction, and the elapsed +8 by its size, against the length +12. So it is playback speed. 65536 is the normal value: player +600 and +200 are 65536 in slots 1, 2, 3, 7, 10. Scripts pass 65536*0.5 (158 times), 0.7 (72), 1 (12), 0.4 (10): L02/1586, L00/1599. Not seen on screen.

fn40(on[, a2]): sets r13-21900, which 0x80008520 and 0x80050B94 give to 0x801E7954: draws two bars of height 75 at y 0 and y 405 in colour 0x000000FF, 806 wide at x -83 if r13-24660 is 1, else 640 wide at x 0. 0x800294BC and 0x800BFFF8 skip work while it's set. a2 goes to r13-21768, which no code reads by that address. Any other count of arguments writes a stale register there. fn40(1,255) is script 2267, fn40(0,0) 2269, fn40(1) and (0) L10/793. fn22's 0x80042974 also sets it, as do 0x801C36AC, 0x801C3768, 0x801C71B0, 0x801D089C, 0x801D08D8. What starts 2267: not found (no script names it, no region in rooms.json; li r3, 2267 at 0x8007BAE8 and 0x8008411C are thing lookups)

fn41(name hash, mode): sets a mode on texture animations of that name in the loaded rooms (0x801EAA2C, 0x801EA82C, 272-byte records). Modes 0x801661FC: 0 restart, 1 pause, 2 stop at end, 3 play once from start, 4 jump to end, 5 resume, 6 loop from frame 1, 7 clear all (bits read in 0x801EA640); above 7 leaves stack values. All 60 literal hashes in scripts are .IFL names in room files, recomputed with 0x801DBC84's hash over every Rooms/rmed*.bpe (build/ed-db/facts/skeptic08/ifl.py), e.g. FLASH01.IFL; 31 calls pass a table value, not checked. primitives.tsv's go_room_a is wrong

fn42(IFL name hash, frame, script): sets the script to run when that animated texture list (.IFL) steps to that frame. 0x8016642C -> 0x801EACA0 walks both loaded areas (0x80155130(0),(1)), matches the name in the 272-byte records (area+20, count area+18) and, if frame < rec+258, writes the script to the u16 array rec+268 at index frame (0x801EA7DC-0x801EA7F0). The tick, on stepping a frame (0x801EA69C-0x801EA700), reads that array and calls 0x801642D4(script,0,0) if it is nonzero (0x801EA704-0x801EA720). Lowered from proved: the firing is read only, and none of the 14 saves holds a nonzero script in its loaded areas' records. The hashes are checked: the name hash 0x801DBC84 ported gives Camera01=565170590; then 718883989 = DB_PNTING_MORPH00.IFL in room 68, 942644835 = RI_MORPHWOMAN00.IFL and 2698102429 = RI_MORPHMAN00.IFL in room 245, 1120396427 = ELECTRIC0001.IFL in room 10 (names in the expanded Rooms/rmed*.bpe). L00/1546: fn41(718883989,5) fn42(718883989,11,1541); script 1541 is fn41(718883989,1). So fn41 (0x801662BC -> 0x801EAA2C, the same area walk) is this IFL system and its go_room_a name looks wrong. 48 calls, 13 script ids (21 counting each level).

fn44(position pointer, r, g, b, a, kind, a7 frames, a8, a9, a10), no return. Fills a record (0x801460E4), a7 at +44, a8 low 16 bits at +4, a9 at +12, a10 at +16, +72 = 0x801F2038. 0x80145EAC(rec, kind): kind 1 sets floats 0, 0, 2 and +72 = 0x80145E1C; kind 2 sets 2000, 0.2, 0.02 and keeps 0x801F2038; others nothing. 0x801458A0(0, rec) takes one of 12 records in the pool 0x80604E90 (r13-21680 in slot1) by 0x801F1D84; 0x801F29F0 copies a7 to +36, a8 to +68, a9 to +8, a10 to +12, rgba to +64, +72 to +108, and the pool step calls +108 (0x801F28D8). 0x801F2038 starts the fade (0x801F27A4) once age +38 reaches +36. Kind 1's 0x80145E1C first adds a10 to +68 each run, capped at a9, then fades. The function at 0x801E6244 takes the pool's count and base (0x801F19A0, 0x801F1988), and its callee 0x801E54BC gives +12 of a stack list to GXInitLightColor (0x801E5578): copying the pool into that list isn't traced, so light is read this far. fn44(L7, 255,50,100,255, 1, 420, 0, 200000, 500) in L09/2004, colour by ed17(), with fn36(420). What +68 does to the light: not traced
